card.title: Origin of life and the proof — Miller–Urey to Archaeopteryx

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Evolution answers two questions with one framework. Where did life come from? Chemical evolution — Oparin–Haldane's reducing early atmosphere built organics, then polymers, then coacervate proto-cells, then self-replication, and Miller–Urey (1953) made the first step in a flask. How do we know descent happened? Five independent evidence lines — morphology, anatomy, fossils, embryology and biochemistry — plus the theories that explain them: Lamarck → Darwin → neo-Darwinism.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Chemical evolution: inorganic (CH₄, NH₃, H₂O, H₂; no O₂) → simple organics (amino acids, sugars, bases) → polymers → proto-cells (coacervates) → self-replicating systems  ·  Miller–Urey: electric discharge + reducing atmosphere → amino acids  ·  Homologous = same structure, different function (divergent); analogous = different structure, same function (convergent)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The origin story needs an oxygen-free, reducing atmosphere — free O₂ would oxidise the new organics before they could assemble — plus an energy source (lightning, UV, volcanic heat) and water to concentrate them. In the evidence lines: fossils need hard parts and rapid burial; homology must be judged on structure and common origin, not on appearance or use; molecular comparisons assume a roughly steady mutation rate (the molecular clock).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Abiogenesis is NOT spontaneous generation — Pasteur killed that idea; abiogenesis means slow chemical evolution over millions of years (the standard trick question). Wings of a bird and a bat are analogous (same job, different origin) while the forelimbs of whale, bat and human are homologous (same bones, different jobs). Vestigial leftovers — appendix, coccyx, pelvic bones in whales. Archaeopteryx carries reptile and bird features together, a true transitional fossil. RNA world: ribozymes both store information and catalyse. Genetic drift is random; selection is not.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Classify any pair by asking 'same structure or same function?': bird wing vs insect wing → analogous; whale flipper vs human arm → homologous; human appendix → vestigial; cytochrome c similarity across species → molecular. Theories test: giraffe neck — Lamarck says stretching during life was inherited; Darwin says longer-necked variants already existed and survived better; neo-Darwinism names the mechanism: selection changing allele frequencies across generations.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Miller–Urey makes amino acids, not a self-replicating cell — no experiment yet links the last chemical step to the first organism, and chirality (why life uses only left-handed amino acids) is unexplained. The fossil record is biased toward hard-bodied, buried organisms. Molecular clocks carry calibration error, and Lamarckism is kept in textbooks mainly as the rejected alternative — useful contrast, not current science.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Derive natural selection in four moves: variation already exists in a population → overproduction makes resources limiting → a struggle follows → the variants that survive and reproduce pass their alleles on, so allele frequencies shift and the population evolves. Derive the RNA world from a chicken-and-egg: proteins need RNA to be built, RNA needs proteins to be copied — unless one molecule does both, which catalytic RNA (ribozyme) does.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Four one-liners carry the unit: 'abiogenesis ≠ spontaneous generation'; 'homo = same origin, ana = same function'; 'vestigial = a leftover vest'; 'Lamarck learned-and-acquired is wrong, Darwin's D-N-S survives'. Chemical evolution stages = O-P-C-S (organics, polymers, coacervates, self-replication). For experiments always write setup → conditions → result → significance, four lines, in that order.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style (unit practice bank): explain the Oparin–Haldane theory in four stages; describe Miller–Urey's experiment with setup, conditions and results; state the RNA-world hypothesis; differentiate homologous from analogous organs with two examples each; explain vestigial organs and Archaeopteryx as evidence; compare Lamarckism and Darwinism; describe neo-Darwinism (modern synthesis) and differentiate natural selection from genetic drift.
